narrative.heading: Taking heart education into the community
narrative.text: Holly Andersen’s education work reaches beyond the cardiology office. NewYork-Presbyterian’s 2017 campaign announcement identifies her as the leader of its hands-only CPR awareness effort, designed to help ordinary bystanders learn how to respond. Her practice biography also describes launching HeartSmarts, a community outreach program. These projects give a concrete view of her interest in public heart-health education.

narrative.heading: Teaching, music and making things
narrative.text: Allison Dobry’s UCSF biography pairs her work with complex skin conditions with teaching dermatology residents at the Veterans Health Administration in San Francisco. Outside work, the same account describes discovering new music, reading fiction and finding new knitting and crochet projects. These documented interests add a personal dimension alongside her clinical and teaching work.

narrative.heading: Access to care and time outdoors
narrative.text: Amanda Twigg’s UCSF biography describes research into teledermatology and its potential to improve access in rural areas, alongside an interest in educating dermatology residents. Away from work, she enjoys San Francisco places such as Ocean Beach, Lands End and Golden Gate Park, with hiking, whale-watching and bird-watching among her activities. Her profile also describes her as an amateur baker.
